Precedent

Context

Precedent checks proposed AI agent tool calls against a corpus of approved and blocked actions. Its goal is to make an action check inexpensive enough to run on each tool call, with evidence a person can review.

Action representation and retrieval

The system represents an action using the tool name, argument features, input provenance, and harness checks. It uses a local, in-process Moss index for hybrid lexical and semantic retrieval, with a metadata filter that compares actions using the same tool.

ACTION CHECKING PIPELINE

Proposed tool call→Features + provenance→Moss retrieval→Allow / block / escalate
A human decision can be written back into the active index and used on the next check, without a separate reindexing job.

Decision evidence and feedback

The check returns an outcome together with the previous decisions and action evidence behind it. New action shapes can be escalated for review. Human decisions are added to the active corpus so subsequent checks can use them.

The prototype includes an API, an interactive interface, a deterministic demonstration agent, an optional live Gemini agent, and evaluation scripts. The implementation separates featurization, provenance, retrieval, decisions, evidence, and auditing.

Evaluation and limits

The repository contains held-out action sets, latency measurements, and an LLM-judge comparison. The evaluation data is synthetic and does not establish accuracy on production traffic.

The documented same-signature baseline matches the retrieval system on these synthetic sets: explicit features provide much of the decision signal. Retrieval contributes ranked evidence and immediate reuse of human feedback. Provenance is based on value overlap and can miss re-encoded values. This prototype is a review and reliability layer, rather than a complete security boundary.
